notes.title: Patch v1.19
notes.content:
Apologies for the long gap between patches - It's mostly bug fixes and laying the groundwork for future patches.
[list]
[*] Made the game work for 4:3 resolutions
[*] If the player gets stalemated, but they have coins, it no longer counts as a stalemate and the coins are highlighted to show the player they can be used
[*] If the player gets checkmated, but they can remove checkmate with a coin, then it no longer counts as a checkmate and highlights the coin/s that can be used
[*] When a badge that in some way gives a piece a modifier is hovered, the explanation of the modifier is shown in the piece description box so the player can see what the effect does before purchase
[*] The AI now understands (and doesn't break the rules) if there's more than 1 courtesan on the board
[*] The AI now understands how their courtesan works (if they manage to get one via necromancy chess)
[*] You can now give yourself more than one courtesan badge in custom matches or setups
[*] the upgrade in the shop that converts a piece to a special piece, now only affects pieces without a positive modifier (it previously only had a greater chance but wasn't guaranteed to target non-special pieces)
[*] Boss badges are now displayed to the right of the round title so the unstable boss badge description does not cover the explanation of unstable
[*] The "Kill all non-king pieces" win condition now works when the opponent has more than one king, without taking them down to a single king
[*] Added a version number to the main menu
[*] The victory screen for scenarios, now says the correct scenario (previously this was off by 1 due to an indexing issue)
[*] Scenario 2 did not correctly set the egg badges to $10 at game start (it now does)
[*] Fixed a bug where you were given an incorrect move to remove check with a courtesan, if the piece causing check is a dragon king
[*] The en-passant square is now reset when using a coin. There was a small bug where the enemy could accidentally en-passant themselves...
[*] Fixed an issue where ice badges wouldn't appear in the shop with the ice coin badge (may have led to other issues with other badges not showing)
[*] Fixed an issue with the pawn model's normals
[*] If it's your first time starting the game, the default color of your pieces will be blue and your opponent's red. This can be changed in the settings, but I think this is clearer as a default.
[/list]

notes.title: Hotfix for menu Issue

notes.title: Patch 1.17
notes.content:
[list]
[*] The pieces shown on the stats pages now have the correct secondary colour
[*] Poison had a bug where a unit would die to poison even if you had taken them the turn before. Which wouldn't be an issue unless you undo that move...
[*] Optimised the AI some more. When moves take longer than 4 seconds for the AI, the depth of the search decreases. It should only do this in endless mode really when there are a lot of Amazons + poison.
[*] Fixed an issue where clicking on the start button more than once could load in the starting badges more than once.
[*] Added an pawn to setup 2 (the atomic setup). I agree with feedback that this was too difficult for beginners at the start.

notes.title: Patch 1.16
notes.content:
Just a small one with some QOL changes and bug fixes. The next patch or two should be a bit bigger unless any new bugs come up.

[list]
[*] Reflecting bishops didn't die with the atomic badge active, if they made a reflecting take (they now do)
[*] Units that usually originate from badges (such as the vampire), but are not attached to a badge (i.e. they were cloned by another badge), now correctly show that they can be sold
[*] Added a check to ensure the resolution saved in the settings is still available (The monitor used may have changed for example, which could lead to issues)
[*] The game now runs in the background. There were previously issues where alt-tabbing while your opponent was making a move could lead to the AI hanging
[*] Complicated boards should now find a move after 6.5 seconds (if there is a move already found and it's good). If this leads to bad moves being made in these scenarios please let me know on discord.
[*] Undeserved Modifiers now no longer gives your opponent a positive modifier in Necromancy Chess 
[*] QOL change: You can now use the directional arrows in the setup menu to loop back from setup 8 to setup 1 by pressing the right arrow, or from 1 to 8 using the left arrow
[*] QOL change: After exiting a run or losing a run, returning the the new game screen will select the setup you were just using with the same modifiers you were using
[/list]

notes.title: Patch 1.15 - Hotfix for Steamdecks
notes.content: The previous patch enabled a screenreader that should only have activated if you use a screenreader - On steamdeck this activated regarless of whether you use one or not. I've now fixed this.

notes.title: Patch 1.10
notes.content:
I do intend to stop doing daily patches now I believe most of the bugs have been ironed out. I'll be working on improving visibility and some more QOL features next in hopefully a bigger patch, unless some smaller issues are found first.

[list]
[*] Hunters mark now returns $2 per marked piece taken
[*] Fixed an issue where undoing a move to a square created by "Lazy Present" did not return the piece to their original square correctly if you had a full inventory
[*] Fixed an issue where undoing a move that created a new modifier square with "Square Again", did not remove the modified square created
[*] Increased longbowmen to 10 value
[*] Fixed an issue where longbowmen caused checkmate, when it wasn't one
[*] When a coin is picked up with controller, your cursor moves to the board immediately
[*] When you cancel using a coin with a controller, you don't place an arrow
[*] Draging an item to the recycle button using the mouse, and releasing the mouse button, will now activate the button
[*] The duck can move more freely when you're in check. I've tried to still allow checkmates to happen (when your king is pinned and you've been checkmated with a jumping move for example), but there is a chance you could be in a situation with the duck, where moving it reveals a new attacking piece which means there's no way to remove the checkmate... I believe this is preferable to the situation to the alternative and current situation where you can remove checkmate with the duck, but the game doesn't allow it.
[*] Upgrade boost now works with the boost upgrade in the shop
[*] Reflecting bishops no longer add the cell they were standing on to the list of cells they can attack (which sometimes gave the player a checkmate when it wasn't one)
[/list]

notes.title: Chess goes Balatro in brand new rule-bending roguelike, out now on Steam
notes.content:
Despite being over 500 years old at this point, chess has more than endured the test of time. Even now, new stratagems are being developed as the next generation of players continues to plumb its near-bottomless tactical depths. Considering its prominence, it's unsurprising that the basic concept of chess has been ripped apart, spliced with elements of other games, and stitched back together more times than I've lost to my dad at it. Solo developer Marc Makes Games has now dropped his own take, Passant, and - wait a minute, why has a Dragon King just blasted my board?

Read the rest of the story...

RELATED LINKS:
New Steam roguelike Passant is a chess Balatro, and you can try it now

notes.title: Passant is out now!
notes.content: [p]I really hope you enjoy the game, I've worked hard to make the game as good as it can be and I hope you see that too.   If you do enjoy the game please remember to leave a review as it really helps the game reach a wider audience.[/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="_jsccDwZ3ys;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][h2]What's new?[/h2][p]The game expands on the demo with the following:[/p][list][*][p]Stages 4 & 5[/p][/*][*][p]Endless Mode[/p][/*][*][p]8 different setups[/p][/*][*][p]8 different scenarios (setups with unique rules or constraints)[/p][/*][*][p]125 badges (including 8 unlockable badges)[/p][/*][*][p]6 challenge modes for each setup[/p][/*][*][p]a custom match and setup mode[/p][/*][*][p]47 Steam achievements[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]I believe the newer badges are some of the best (especially the unlockable badges) and lead to much better builds than before.[/p][p][/p][h2]What about the demo?[/h2][p]I was intending to remove the demo, as I'd been told it can hurt sales. But I've decided to keep the demo for now as [/p][olist][*][p]I don't want to take it away from people who can't afford the game at the moment.[/p][/*][*][p]I think it's the most consumer friendly approach to let people try before they buy.[/p][/*][/olist][p]I'll update the demo to make it clearer what's missing from the demo when compared to the full game, but apart from that (and some bug fixes) it will stay the same.[/p][p][/p][h2]What's next?[/h2][p]I'll continue fixing bugs as they come up - please report anything, however small, in the bugs channel over on discord.[/p][p][/p][p]I'll also be working on mobile versions, and depending on how well the game does, possibly console ports.  [/p][p][/p][p]I would also love to do a content update at some point as I love the game and still love working on it. Possibly around the time of tabletop fest in January 2026 (which Passant will be a part of!).[/p][p][/p][h2]Thank you[/h2][p]Lastly I just want to say thank you to everyone that's played the demo, given the game a wishlist or been a part of the discord community. I really appreciate it.[/p][p][/p][p]All the best,[/p][p]Marc[/p][p][/p]

notes.title: Passant is launching in 4 days!
notes.content: [p]Just a quick update that Passant is launching on [b]August 11th[/b] (in 4 days)! I'll tease more content over on Discord, but I just want to highlight some of the most recent changes to the game which addresses a lot of the feedback I was getting from the demo.[/p][p][/p][p]First of all, here's a sneak peak of the beginning of the new trailer which shows some new badges and effects:[/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="-8ry7SrO9GM;full"][/previewyoutube][h2]Beginner Mode and AI Improvements[/h2][p]There's now a beginner mode for the AI, that will play unoptimal moves (up to a point). It's probably one of the most fun ways to play if you're just looking to play quick games without too much thought.[/p][p][/p][p]I've also made a lot of improvements to the AI over the last 6-7 months since the demo launched. This includes bug fixes (where the AI would make clearly bad moves or illegal moves), as well as improvements to the AI's understanding of badges and win conditions. Previously the AI was not aware of the multiple check win condition for example, but it now is.[/p][p][/p][p]I want to make a more dedicated post on the AI at some point as it's super interesting.[/p][h2]More Synergy with badges[/h2][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45318449/a186ee6ce2f2f4de223b54356ce1e2dd6ec51a6e.gif"][/img][/p][p]This is one of the things I wish I had more of in the demo. A lot of the new badges synergise with the badges in the demo and vice versa and I've had playtesters surprise me with builds that synergise in ways I hadn't considered, which was pretty cool. [/p][p][/p][p]An example of badges synergising would be:[/p][list][*][p]the new badge that makes square modifier badges trigger twice on match start (or the other that makes them trigger again once used),[/p][/*][*][p]one that makes modifiers gained in a match permanent (alongside various badges that allow you to gain modifiers in a match)[/p][/*][*][p]or two new badges shown in the gif above - 1 spawns useless target dummys when you lose a piece and the other temporarily upgrades pieces next to the king (making them not so useless). This gets even better if you can find a way to gain multiple kings or better kings somehow...[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h2]Difficulty more generally [/h2][p]There have been discussions about the game being 1. too easy and 2. too hard. Obviously the issue is that for beginners it was too hard, but it's maybe been easy for people who play chess regularly. [/p][p]The demo was just a taster, so difficulty does change quite a bit as you add more challenges and reach stages 4 and 5, but I've also made the following changes:[/p][list][*][p]The value of your opponent's setups has been adjusted to make things easier for beginners[/p][/*][*][p]A hard mode which increases the difficulty past the original demo's has been unlocked as a challenge mode by default (this makes more of a difference in stages 4 and 5)[/p][/*][*][p]There's now a beginner AI level - As discussed above[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h2]New languages[/h2][p]I've added Spanish, French and Brazilian Portuguese translations (alongside the existing English, German, Russian, Traditional Chinese and Simplified Chinese translation). If you find any issues with these please let me know over on the discord.[/p][h2][/h2][p]Thanks for reading and let me know if you have any questions. I'm most available over on Discord, but I'll try to monitor the comments here as long as possible.[/p][p][/p][p]All the best,[/p][p]Marc[/p][p][/p][p][/p]

notes.title: Demo Updates and Steam Next Fest
notes.content:
It’s been a while since I’ve posted an update here, but for the last 4 months since the demo launched I’ve been consistently patching it with bug-fixes and content updates. More detailed patch notes are usually posted on Discord, but I want to take some time to point out the high level changes. 

I also want to mention that the game will be part of June's next fest and will be launching shortly after this in August, though the exact date is still to be confirmed. I've been working to make sure the demo is great, but also to make sure there's a lot of additional content when the game launches, and I can't wait for people to get their hands on the new setups, badges and endless mode.

[h2]The Cannon Badge and Other New Badges[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45318449/67a90f98d04dda4199c887f729edc1b08ec6b2f8.gif[/img]
Over the last couple of months I’ve added around 9 additional badges (bringing the total in the demo to 61). The most recent is a badge that adds a unique piece called the cannon. The cannon takes like a rook, but creates an explosion where it takes and moves a square backwards from its starting position, killing whatever piece was behind it, or flying off the board if it’s at the edge.

[h2]Piece Modifiers and Upgrades[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45318449/2ed9adc659e64ad36e31ad1bcf46959e7cdddf4a.gif[/img]
Pieces can now have a modifier applied that changes the way they work, either for the better or worse. Pieces can appear in the shop with these modifiers (though you get a discount for unstable and mercenary pieces), an upgrade in the shop can add a modifier to a random piece, or certain badges can add or remove modifiers.

[h2]Shop changes[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45318449/e02107ef4145335727cd4e10fba7e0ab046798f6.gif[/img]
I’ve added upgrades to the shop which appear instead of coins. These can either upgrade the lowest value piece to a higher value one, give a piece a random modifier or give the player a way to gain more money over time. There's also an emergency pawn button to give access to pawns at an increased cost (for emergencies). The idea behind these changes it to allow the player to always have an opportunity to incrementally improve their build.

[h2]AI Changes[/h2]
I’ve been constantly updating the AI for the past few months. When the demo originally launched I used fairy stockfish - a separate program that the game communicated with the give the best move by the AI. The problem was that some of the modifiers or pieces could not be supported, so the AI would be great until something it couldn't understand correctly was added to the board (the courtesan piece as an example). For this reason I wrote my own chess engine around a month after the demo launched, which can accommodate some weirder (or less balanced) pieces and badges. An example of this is the cannon piece, which wouldn't be possible if I was relying on a third party chess engine.

I’ve been improving the engine and recently made a big step forward in terms of efficiency and level of plays - Especially when the atomic badge is in use. I’ve also made the easy difficulty select an in-optimal move now (as long as it isn’t sacrificing pieces etc), which should make things easier for beginners. If you want the extra challenge you can increase AI difficulty in the settings menu.

[h2]Visuals[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45318449/c402ae87dd692e8b77c3a4bfc6190014072a5488.png[/img]
I’ve changed the styling of the board and UI recently and I think it looks much better and clearer. I’m also adding more effects where possible to make things more interesting.

[h2]Tutorial[/h2]
I’ve added a new tutorial which starts the first time the game is played. This should hopefully give enough context to complete beginners of chess to be able to figure things out as they play. If you’ve already played or don’t like tutorials, it can also be skipped using the pause menu. Alternatively you can also replay it from the settings menu.

[h2]Languages[/h2]
Over the next couple of days I’m adding support to the demo for German, Traditional Chinese, Simplified Chinese and Russian. The game will use these languages if your steam language is set to these (otherwise it will default to English).

notes.title: Demo Update 15/02/2025
notes.content:
Firstly, I want to say thank you to everyone that has been playing the game and also to everyone reporting bugs on the discord channel, it's really helping to improve the game.

With that said here are the patch notes for the most recent update to the demo. There are smaller patches I've released to fix game breaking bugs (which I've not been posting about here but have posted on Discord), but seeing as this is quite a large one I've posted the patch notes below.

[h2]Changed/Added content[/h2]
[list]
[*] Reworked the AI entirely - A custom solution is now used which fixes edge cases. For example the AI now correctly understands the courtesan and reflecting bishops.
[/list]

The AI may be slightly weaker in standard chess positions, but should be stronger in edge cases/ be harder to break. As this is the first time the AI is being tested publicly, if there are any issues with it or strange moves taken by the AI then please let me know in the bug channel on discord. I'll continue to improve the AI over time - for example it will be possible in a future update to give the AI an understanding of the player's win conditions, so the opponent shouldn't allow the player to win using the no capture condition as easily.

There are now only 3 levels of AI - The middle level (challenging) is now the default level and the most tested so I would recommend using this. The easy level will likely make clear blunders, and the max setting, although it calculates more moves, may not actually increase the difficulty (but likely will increase the enemy's turn time).

I'm also pretty excited about the change too as it opens up a lot of possibilities - For example, atomic chess previously was either on or off for all pieces. Now I could theoretically allow one piece to be atomic while others are not.

[list]
[*] Removed the challenge level that deleted pieces lost on board
[*] Added 2 new optional challenge levels to unlock - 1. non-pawn/men are restricted to your first rank and 2. Rewards are $1 less
[*] Changed the challenge system - challenge modes can be unlocked by completing different criteria + Multiple can be selected at once - In the full game there will be 6 challenge modes and all can be enabled at once (if you wanted!)
[/list]

[h2]Balance changes[/h2]
[list]
[*] The "Pass them on" badge now only gives $1 for each undo remaining
[*] The target badge now only gives $1 for each target killed
[*] The Buffalo no longer has a zebra move.
[/list]
 
[h2]Bug fixes[/h2]
[list]
[*] Frozen pieces no longer pin player pieces between the frozen piece and the player king
[*] Pieces chained by the courtesan no longer pin player pieces between the frozen piece and the player king
[*] The dragon king now shows the correct possible moves if attacked by a bishop or rook
[*] Fixed a bug where the game sometimes wouldn't recognise the player having no possible moves
[*] Fixed some wording issues
[*] Fixed multiple bugs with badges failing while activating
[*] The SUGNOMA and Free Real Estate badges now work correctly with the Lost Coins badge
[*] Fixed a bug where getting the double king badge after getting the dragon king badge, did not give 2 dragon kings
[*] Fixed a bug where the badges that give coins, did not update the text for how many coins were held
[*] Fixed a bug where the checkmate light would remain green after a checkmate
[*] Picking up badges while loading a match is no longer possible - This fixes a bug where you could pick up the atomic chess badge while loading so the opponents pieces are not advanced a rank
[/list]
 
[h2]To come (for the demo)[/h2]
[list]
I'll likely be adding these as smaller patches over the next few days:
[*] AI improvements
[*] Inevitable bug fixes
[*] Adding juice to the UI
[*] I still need to fix the bug where the chain sound plays when a king moving around a courtesan
[/list]

Also as a warning - The new update will delete any active save (as I've had to update save files to work with the new challenge system), so if you're on a run you want to complete, hold back on the download if possible. This update is hopefully the last time I will have to do this for the demo.

notes.title: New Steam roguelike Passant is a chess Balatro, and you can try it now
notes.content:
Balatro proved that with enough thought, anything can become a roguelike. It doesn't matter if you've got a deck of cards, mahjong tiles, or just some dice, because all of them can be turned into an endlessly replayable loop of utter perfection. While I love the combat-focused Hades, Enter the Gungeon, and Dead Cells, these aren't the only forms a roguelike can take. In fact, it turns out you can take something as ubiquitous as chess, and put it right in the middle of the genre. This is exactly what Passant does, and its brand-new demo already has me hooked.

notes.title: Game Update #2
notes.content:
Hi All!

The demo for Passant will be launching on steam on January 28th!

The demo is now in the final testing phase. I've created a final version of the demo but I just want to get some playtesters to run through it and find any bugs, before releasing it to the world on steam.

If you do want to play right now - you can [url=https://discord.gg/WRMt6mSah3]join the discord[/url] and download the current version of the demo from the "Updates" section. But please do provide feedback in the discord if you find any bugs. I'm also looking for feedback on difficulty and general game feel.

I will also open up a playtest of the game on Steam in the next 3-5 days (once steam approves it), so watch out for that.

[h3]Further Info about the demo
[/h3]
I mentioned it in the last update, but there will be 2 starting setups in the demo (these are the badges, pieces and coins you start with). There are also 2 challenge levels, which are extra levels of difficulty you unlock after completing a run, which as you might expect, provide an extra level of challenge. I've now nailed down what these will be in the demo.
[olist]
[*]The 1st challenge level is the base version of the game.
[*]The second one unlocks after completing the demo once and makes it so pieces you lose in the game are permanently lost from your setup board. In the actual game this will likely be the last/hardest challenge level, as it completely changes the way you play and is extremely punishing.
[/olist]
There will of course be a larger number of starting setups in the full game and 6 different challenge levels.

[h3]Further Info about the chess AI
[/h3]
I'd like to use these updates to explain how certain areas of the game work. If you want to know something specific then please let me know in the comments, but this time I'd like to talk about the AI in the game.

The AI in Passant works by, at the start of your opponent's turn, feeding the current board state into a separate chess engine. This can give the AI the best possible move, but is modulated depending on the difficulty level selected (easy by default) by changing the number of moves ahead the engine considers. 

The game comes with Fairy Stockfish (a chess engine that understands different rulesets) but theoretically a player could replace this, as it's a separate file that gets executed by the game (though it would need to understand the same rules).

The current rules of a match are fed into the chess engine using a .ini file, which the game actively edits as new badges and pieces are added. Fairy stockfish reads this .ini file so it is always aware of the rules and plays accordingly.

There are a small number of items or unique pieces which the chess AI is not aware of. An example of this is the vampire piece, which is a unique piece that can move/take any square up to 2 steps away, but becomes the piece it takes. The engine is aware of the movement of this piece, but not its ability to become the piece it takes. Because it's a unique piece I think abilities like this are fine and don't become too overpowered. Though I am keeping an eye on this and may restrict the use of abilities that the AI isn't aware of in one of the challenge levels.

If you have any other questions, please let me know below!

All the best,
Marc

notes.title: Game Update #1
notes.content:
Hi All! This is the first post for (hopefully) a weekly developer update going forward. I'll talk more about the full game in later posts, but for today I'd like to talk a bit about the upcoming demo for Passant.

[h3]Demo Progress[/h3]
The demo is pretty much complete. I'm testing it currently to make sure there aren't any game breaking bugs and that it's actually fun... The difficulty is making the demo fun for players of all abilities. It needs to be easy enough for beginners/novices to get started, but provide a challenge for experts if they want it. 

If you'd like to help test it, I'll be sharing a version of it on discord over the next few days (before a steam version launches at the end of the month).

[url=https://discord.gg/WRMt6mSah3]Click here to join the Discord![/url]

[h3]Demo Difficulty[/h3]
As it's just a demo, the base game will be set quite easy (as mentioned above), but I will likely provide a challenge mode for experts to stretch themselves once they've completed the demo once. There's also an option in the settings to adjust AI difficulty (which is set to easy by default).

[h3]Demo Scope[/h3]
In terms of scope, the demo will give access to the first 3 stages (out of 5 total + an endless mode in the full game). It'll also have 2 different starting setups, which are the pieces, the modifiers (badges) and the usable items (coins) that you start with.

I'll include all the current badges (game modifiers), which totals around 60 currently. These can be purchased in the store in between matches.

[h3]Steam deck compatibility [/h3]
This is an announcement that Passant will fully support the Steam Deck. I've built the game from the ground up to work on the steam deck and controllers and I've been mainly testing the game this way.

[h3]Game Showcase Video[/h3]
I've been working on a new trailer for the game and accidentally created more of a showcase of some of the badges. You can check it out on youtube below!

[previewyoutube=jYs1GvOwZ9s;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3]Questions?[/h3]
If you have any questions please comment below and I can answer directly or cover it in a future update :)
